recentItems.title: Classic potential? £1m buy First Law remains unbeaten | Full Race | Racing TV
recentItems.description:
Godolphin are hoping lightning strikes twice after First Law kept his unbeaten record intact in the Listed Betfair Celebrates Bow Echo Ascendant Stakes, a race won 12 months ago by this year’s star miler. 

Bow Echo landed the Haydock contest on his second start as a two-year-old and went on to take the mile division by storm this season before a setback led to him being retired to stud after three Group One wins.

Charlie Appleby will be holding high hopes now for the still unbeaten Too Darn Hot colt, after the 6-4 favourite forged clear in the final furlong to win by three-quarters of a length from Rocket Boy. 

Winning jockey William Buick suggested First Law, like Bow Echo last season, would aim to maintain his unbeaten two-year-old record in the Emirates Autumn Stakes at Newmarket on October 10.

recentItems.title: Almeraq is all class in Betfair Sprint Cup! | Full Race | Racing TV
recentItems.description:
Almeraq left an off-day at Newmarket clearly in the rearview mirror with a dominating victory in the Betfair Sprint Cup at Haydock Park.

Last year’s winner Big Mojo flew out of the stalls and set the early pace alongside Marvelman, before the race began to get serious two furlongs out.

Paborus had travelled sweetly when he arrived on the scene – but as soon as Almeraq began to assert in the hands of regular pilot Tom Marquand it was all over, as the 9-4 favourite turned on the afterburners to leave the field in his wake, powering away for a four-and-a-quarter-length victory.

recentItems.title: Constitution Hill takes fourth behind Pride Of Arras at Kempton | Full Race | Racing TV
recentItems.description:
Constitution Hill had to settle for an ultimately well-beaten fourth to Pride Of Arras on his eagerly-awaited third Flat outing in the William Hill September Stakes at Kempton Park.

So brilliant at his peak in his hurdling days, Nicky Henderson’s superstar has remained one of racing’s biggest draws since switching to the level – but this Group Three affair was a major step up from his victories at Southwell and at this track in February and March respectively.

As the odds-on Gethin took early command of the mile-and-a-half contest, Billy Loughnane and Constitution Hill (9-2) sat in a close-up fourth and were still travelling with a degree of menace turning for home.

Asked for his effort just outside the two-furlong pole, there was only a flattering moment of hope before it became clear he was not going to get involved and instead it was the Ralph Beckett-trained Pride Of Arras (11-2) who swept to the front, holding off the rallying Gethin by a length.

Constitution Hill had arrived at Kempton with the Melbourne Cup a tantalising option for the autumn, but Henderson will now return to the drawing board and said: “Melbourne is gone now sadly. Today was always going to tell us what we were going to do next and I suppose he’s posing us another question now.

“I don’t think we want to go under a mile and a half, that is for sure, and 12, 13 or 14 furlongs seems to be the range of where we go with him. I do think he is going to come on for the run, what with the way he got there as if it was going to happen, but from a furlong out I think he took a bit of a blow. It will sharpen him up.

“He’s going to be eligible to run in handicaps now and it will be interesting to see what the reaction on Tuesday is. It could allow him into some very lucrative handicaps in England, Ireland or wherever you like.

“From two novice stakes of very differing strength and depth it was a big step today and we’ll now just wait to see what it does for his mark.”

He added: “We’ll find a nice race for him somewhere and he’s by no means finished yet, I can promise you that.”

Australian dreams may have been crushed for Constitution Hill, but for connections of the winner Pride Of Arras, a trip to Canada is now on the cards as last year’s Dante and Great Voltigeur scorer showed his class on the Sunbury synthetics.

Beckett said: “He’s a good horse and was good in the Dante and Voltigeur last year and a talented individual.

“He had a really bad foot problem that came to light just before the John Porter and he wasn’t really ready when he ran against Calandagan in the Grand Prix de Saint-Cloud, but I had to run him somewhere.

“I then thought he lugged out when second (to Item) in the York Stakes and was still thinking about his foot.

“I thought he looked a million dollars before the International and hadn’t looked better. It was a great disappointment to all of us we couldn’t run at York. They loaded him at York before all the other horses had gone behind and I’d say he was looking at the horses walking towards him and that’s what set him off

“I thought today he would probably find the surface a touch deeper than he would like so you could probably upgrade it a little bit.

“I think there is a good chance he will really enjoy Toronto when we take him to the Canadian International.”

On the impact of Constitution Hill at Kempton, Beckett added: “It’s great that the crowds have come out and we’re in the entertainment business, but inevitably you have to worry about your own horse.

“I’m delighted there is a crowd and it was a good race. The first two are good horses and Constitution Hill wasn’t disgraced.”

recentItems.title: Gavin Lynch: 25 Years Of Betting | On The Wire On The Road
recentItems.description:
Andrew Blair White is on the road for a new three-part series around Irish racing, and he begins in Dublin with Gavin Lynch.

Gavin has been betting for twenty-five years, and three years ago he stopped doing it on the flat altogether. He explains why, what giving up Dundalk taught him first, and why arriving fresh in October beats grinding through a summer.

He talks about his father, a small trainer who ran a horse into third in the Triumph Hurdle and took him racing every Saturday from the age of six. About the year he spent as a bookmaker after coming home from Australia, standing up at Thurles waiting for someone to whisper him a winner that never came. 

Gavin explains why the worst opinion you can have is half an opinion, why every punter should keep a P&L, why specialising beats spreading yourself across five sports. He also looks back on five years of Upping The Ante with David Jennings, and talks about the members' service he runs now from November to March.

Then off to Bellewstown, celebrating 300 years of racing, where Gavin has three hours of form study behind him and €300 to play with and all of it going to the Curragh to Curragh Charity Cycle.
